Latin-transliterated Medi stretches: 31:49, 37:56-38:10, 39:08-39:25, 40:22-40:32, 41:01, 41:44, 42:37-42:52, 48:48-49:42, 52:47-53:19, 54:20, 55:06-55:40, 56:37, 59:44, 1:00:47, 1:08:03-1:08:15, 1:09:04, 1:09:55, 1:10:32. English-only stretches: 13:22-13:55 (sirens), 36:13-37:29 (proficiency test), 1:08:27-1:09:02. rows.medi_said: What is... stressed? / I don't know. ما بتذكر.
rows.why: He could not produce the word for stressed (said ما بتذكر); Amal supplied مضغوط - a didn't-know, not on her sheet.

rows.medi_said: إنتِ متأكد إنه أنا أتعلم-- بتعلمه؟
rows.why: Addressing Amal (إنتِ) he used the masculine adjective متأكد; she only answered 'أنا متأكدة' naturally, no correction voiced.
rows.english: Are you sure that I learned it?

rows.why: He asked whether he had (already) learned the word using the present بتعلمه; Amal recast in the past تعلمتها.

rows.medi_said: Would you say أنا كامل نسيتو؟ ... can you say كامل نسيتو؟ like completely forgot.
rows.why: He asked if كامل (whole) works for 'completely'; Amal said no and supplied كليًا - a didn't-know asked as a question.
He repeated her 'when we review the emotions' with the wrong verb person (راجع) and no el-; she recast نراجع الـ and drilled نراجع.
Asked which season it is (Sept 21), he said ربيع (spring); she said 'مش ربيع، لا' and supplied خريف - sheet row 'autumn / fall | 5areef | خريف'.
بنطلون is masculine; he used the feminine خضرا and Amal recast أخضر, which he repeated.
Talking about his own city's weather he said عندهم (they have); Amal recast عنا (we have) and he repeated عندنا.
After 11+ the noun is singular; Amal echoed تلاتين as a prompt, he fixed to يوم and she named 'after ten, يوم'.

rows.amal_said: آه، يعني نحتاج الـ jacket إندم.
rows.why: English jacket inside an Arabic sentence while the word is on her sheet: 'jacket | Jakait | جاكيت | jakait'; Amal let it pass (used jacket herself) - pre-ruled do-not-correct (AR-1933).

rows.medi_said: نحتاج، um, jacket. / We only have thirty days that we need a jacket
rows.amal_said: آه، يعني نحتاج الـ jacket إندم. ... on them، بس يعني إندم in Arabic.
rows.why: For 'thirty days that we need a jacket' Amal recast with الـ and a pointer back to the days (فيهم 'in them'), explaining 'on them'; he repeated فيهم.
rows.english: (thirty days) in which we need the jacket

rows.why: The subject is the thirty days (plural); Amal prompted in English 'They change.' and he changed to بتغيروا (her typed byet8ayyaru).

rows.medi_said: أكلت الـ pizza ضل آآآ الـ آخر الأسبوع.
rows.amal_said: The pizza that remained. That remained from أخر الأسبوع.
rows.chat: akalet el-pizza illi dallat min 2aa5er el-usboo3
rows.why: No اللي before the relative verb; Amal rephrased 'The pizza that remained' and he rebuilt 'الـ pizza اللي ...'.
rows.english: the pizza that was left over from the weekend

rows.why: aa5er + el- + noun = the end of; el- never goes on aa5er. Amal recast 'أخر الأسبوع' (and 'from'), dropping his el-.

rows.medi_said: لما إشي بيصير كل الـ fire department و ambulance آآآ آجوا.
rows.why: A habit ('usually when something happens they all come') needs the b- present; he used past آجوا and Amal recast بيجو.
lamma drops the b- on the next verb; he kept بيصير and Amal did not address it (her fix was on آجوا).

rows.amal_said: One piece. Pizza is one. ... Pizza is woman. ... feminine.
rows.why: The verb must agree with pizza (feminine singular); he said دلوا (plural), Amal named 'Pizza is one... feminine' and he produced ضلت.
The set phrase for craving is جاي على بالي; he said جاي لي (and dropped كان), Amal recast and he repeated 'جاي ع بالي pizza'.
Adjective goes after the noun; he put الحرام first. Amal only echoed الحرام laughing; her chat has el-peporony el-7araam. Chat alone is not a correction.

rows.medi_said: آآآ أنا ما بحب الـ، الفلفل حلو
rows.amal_said: ولا أنا ما بحب الحلو. بحب البحري. ما بحب الفلفل الحلو.
rows.why: Noun phrase 'the sweet pepper' needs el- on the adjective too (otherwise 'the pepper is sweet'); Amal recast 'الفلفل الحلو'.
Wrong pattern of a sheet word ('dry | Naashef | ناشف'); Amal said and typed ناشف, he repeated it.

rows.medi_said: So if you ask for a pastry, do you say واحد حلو؟ حلوة؟ أو وحدة حلوة؟
rows.amal_said: يعني كعكة. ... بسكوتة، كعكة، خلص احكي Pastry.
rows.why: He asked how to order a pastry; Amal supplied كعكة / بسكوتة - a didn't-know.

rows.medi_said: أنا راح أستانك. أستانك. Yeah, أستانك.
rows.why: Wrong shape of استنى (sheet 'he waited | huwwe stanna'); Amal recast استناك and he repeated أستناكِ (her chat astannaaki).
'Its price' needs the owner ending on حق, not el-; Amal prompted 'Its price' and he added an ending (حقو).
The ending must point to the coffee (feminine); he used -o, Amal said 'قديش حقها. Cuz it's coffee.' and he repeated حقها.
ra7 takes a bare verb (أقدر), he kept the b-; Amal let it pass and her chat simply drops ra7 (ba2dar adfa3).

rows.amal_said: أدفع. You use the credit card to pay. So what do you use? Which preposition? ... B. Credit card.
rows.why: Paying with an instrument takes bi-, not ma3; Amal asked which preposition, said B, and he produced أدفع بالـ credit card.

rows.medi_said: أدفع أطفالهم (engine wrote أطفالهم = adfa3 lahom) / Do I still need to say أدفع لهم؟
rows.amal_said: لا. ... If it's for them it would mean شو؟ Pay for. ... أدفع عن.
rows.right: أدفع (لك) بالـ credit card; pay for = أدفع عن
rows.why: He said adfa3 lahom (engine wrote أطفالهم) to the barista; Amal said لا and explained دفع takes لـ for the payee and عن for 'pay for', so لهم was wrong here.

rows.amal_said: You were right هذي الأكلة. هذي is for feminine.
rows.why: أكلة is feminine; he switched to هذا and Amal named 'هذي is for feminine', he repeated هذي الأكلة.

rows.chat: haadi el-akle mish taaza u mish zaakye
rows.why: The subject is الأكلة (feminine); he used masculine زاكي, Amal let it pass vocally (her chat has zaakye).

rows.amal_said: It's like sir. We learned it.
rows.why: He did not know the meaning of her أستاذ (ما بعرف); she supplied 'sir' - comprehension didn't-know.

rows.amal_said: It's like شو مالك؟ شو مالك؟ شو مال الشاورما؟
rows.why: He did not understand شو مال (asked 'مال is...'); Amal explained via شو مالك - comprehension didn't-know.

rows.medi_said: طعم، uh, طعمها مرة و حامضة
rows.amal_said: said first. ... خلص إنت هلأ you're now describing the taste so it's more.
rows.why: The adjectives describe طعم (masculine); he switched to feminine مرة/حامضة, Amal said what he said first was right because he is describing the taste, he repeated 'tam mur oo hamid'.
rows.english: its taste is bitter and sour

rows.why: Repeating her بيهمنا he said بيهنّا; she corrected 'بهم، بيهمنا' (sheet 'i matter | Bahemm | بهم').

rows.medi_said: so if I say I'm famous at cooking, would it be a-ana mash-mashhur bi-ut-bi atbuk without the bi, right?
rows.amal_said: في. في or be. في، mm, the noun. Noun is طبخ.
rows.why: After bi/fi use the noun of the action, not a verb; Amal named 'the noun. Noun is طبخ' and he said 'Bi طبخ الكباب' (framed as a question, but he attempted atbuk).

rows.medi_said: أنا بظن إنه هادي مش لازم
rows.amal_said: مش لا-- إنه ما كان لازم، صح.
rows.chat: bas ana bazonn enno ma kaan laazem
rows.why: 'It wasn't necessary' (his mother taught him to wash rice) needs kaan + laazem; Amal recast ما كان لازم and he repeated it.

rows.medi_said: uh, is not, yeah, mish il-roz fi Iran.
rows.chat: el-ruzz hoan mish zayy el-ruzz bi Iran
rows.why: He left out زي (like); Amal prompted 'it's not like' and he added زي.
rows.english: the rice here is not like the rice in Iran

rows.why: The subject الشركة is feminine; he used the he/they form, Amal said 'بتبيع because شركة is' and he finished 'feminine. بتبيع'.
Same feminine subject (الشركة) right after the rule; he said بيغسل, Amal recast بتغسل and he repeated it.

rows.amal_said: لا، لا، لا. ما بيطبخه، بيخليه...
rows.why: مي is feminine (she had just said بمي سخنة) and 'the hot water' needs el- on the adjective; her لا answered the cooking question, not the form.
rows.english: won't the hot water cook it?

rows.why: A habit ('sometimes when I'm lazy') needs bakoon; Amal prompted 'بكون' and he said 'Lama ana bakun kasul'.
Plain present habit needs b-; he said أستعمل twice, Amal recast بستعمل.

rows.amal_said: ماكينة. We didn't learn ماكينة. ... ماكينة الرز.
rows.why: He fell back to English; Amal supplied ماكينة الرز and said they had not learned ماكينة - a didn't-know.
Plain present needs b-; Amal recast بعمله and he repeated it.
طريق is road; the method is طريقة (sheet 'way / method | Tariqa | طريقة' vs 'road / way / route | 6ariq | طريق'); Amal recast and he repeated الطريقة.
طريقة is feminine and 'the long way' needs el- on the adjective; Amal said only mm-hmm (chat el-tari2a el-taweela).
Plain present step in a recipe needs b-; Amal recast بطبخه and he repeated it.
11+ takes a singular noun; Amal echoed عشرين as a prompt and he fixed to دقيقة.
Wrong form of a sheet word ('butter | Zibdeh | زبدة'); Amal recast زبدة (and again at 46:53 when he repeated زبداية - one row).

rows.medi_said: لازم أحط شوي زيت، uh، في الـ تحت الطنجرة.
rows.chat: laazem a7ut shwai zait fi el-tunjara
rows.why: He put el- on the first word of the phrase (الـ تحت الطنجرة); Amal let it pass.
rows.english: in the bottom of the pot

rows.amal_said: لا، لا تحت is just under. Below. Under. ... what's opposite؟ You know opposite. ... عكس الملعقة.
rows.why: For 'the other end' he used تحت (under) and then الآخر تاني; Amal said لا and led him to عكس (sheet 'opposite | 3aks | عكس').

rows.medi_said: العكس؟ So أنا أستعمل بالعكس المقلاة.
rows.why: مقلاة is a pan, he meant the spoon (sheet 'spoon | Ma3la2a | معلقة', 'pan | Ma2la | مقلى'); Amal recast الملعقة and stressed 'ملعقة spoon'.
Idafa 'the back of the spoon': the first word takes no el-/bi-el-; Amal recast عكس الملعقة and he repeated 'عكس المقلاة'.
rows.english: the opposite end of the spoon

rows.why: Plain present needs b- (she had fixed أستعمل at 43:05); this time she only fixed the noun phrase.

rows.medi_said: Yeah, what was the bixfun? Bixfun was also not that family tree.
rows.why: He asked for the ladle word he could not recall; Amal supplied مغرفة (sheet 'spatula / ladle | Ma8rafa').
قصير means short; low temperature is واطية (sheet 'low | Waati | واطي'); Amal supplied it and he repeated واطية.

rows.medi_said: صوت طويل or صوت قصير نار؟
rows.amal_said: مش صوت. Calm. I guess calm fire then.
rows.why: Asked how to say 'quiet fire' he offered صوت; Amal said مش صوت and led to هادية - a didn't-know asked as a question.
Adjective goes after the noun and agrees (نار is feminine); Amal said نار first, he reordered 'نار هادي؟ هادية' and she confirmed هادية.
مشتهي means craving; cooked/done is مستوي (sheet 'cooked/done (m) | Mistwi'); Amal recast and he repeated مستوي.
For 'the bottom part of the rice' Amal recast الرز من تحت and explained تحت الرز means what is under the rice; he repeated الرز من تحت (and slipped again at 52:40, re-fixed - same moment).
'We Iranians (are known for)' needs el-; Amal recast إحنا الإيرانيين and he repeated it.

rows.medi_said: إه، إحنا إيرانيين uh, مشهور، مشهورين بنحط الـ saffron
rows.why: Same el- drop two minutes after her fix; she did not voice it again (chat has el-iraanyeen).
He used English saffron (not on her sheet); Amal supplied الزعفران - a didn't-know.

rows.medi_said: uh, awali is, awali is country, right?
rows.why: He mangled the sheet word ('country | Dawle | دولة') as awali/دوالي; Amal said دولة and laughed at دوالي.
Talking about Iranian meat (his own people) he again said عندهم; Amal recast عنا and he repeated 'anna'.

rows.medi_said: بس الطعم مشهور uh, من إيران
rows.why: 'The taste famous in Iran' needs fi, not min; Amal said في and he repeated في إيران.
rows.english: the taste that is famous in Iran

rows.why: 3ind is negated with ma, not mish; Amal recast ما عنا and he repeated 'ما عنا أكل بحري'.

rows.medi_said: I agree. Hold on. How do I say I agree?
rows.why: He asked how to say 'I agree'; Amal supplied معك حق - a didn't-know.

rows.amal_said: لا، بس one L. Where do I put the L؟ It's just one.
rows.why: In idafa only the owner takes el-; Amal said لا, only one L, and he fixed to 'ta'am il samak', she said ممتاز.
rows.english: the taste of the fish is spicy

rows.amal_said: أحسن من كل الدنيا؟ ... So أحسن رز في الدنيا، أو بالدنيا.
rows.why: 'The best in the world' is a7san + noun (أحسن رز بالدنيا), not 'better than the world'; Amal asked, recast it, and he repeated أحسن رز بالدنيا.
rows.english: our rice is the best rice in the world

rows.why: 3ind is negated with ma, and 'you (people in Palestine)' is -kom; Amal recast ما عندكم.

rows.medi_said: غريب عشان في الـ دولة زي دولة عربي
rows.why: دولة is feminine; he used masculine عربي and Amal let it pass.
'Many Iranian restaurants' needs the plural مطاعم (she supplies it a minute later); not voiced here.

rows.chat: a7san ma6aa3em Iranyeen fi el-denia fi UAE
rows.why: He meant 'the best Persian restaurants' (plural); Amal prompted 'Restaurants.' and he said مطاعم إيرانيين (also dropping the wrong el- on the adjective).

rows.medi_said: مين بيدفع؟ Hold on. مين بيدفع؟ Who pays?
rows.why: He repeated her 'مين بيفتح' as بيدفع (who pays); Amal corrected 'Opens، بيفتح'.
Asked for the word for conversation he said ما بعرف; Amal supplied محادثة (sheet 'conversation practice | Mu7aadase').
